correctness.rationale: For any compact-support invariant probability on the nonnegative orthant, invariance of antiderivative f(X), f(Y), f(Z) with arbitrary continuous f yields E[Φ(Z)−k4X|X]=0, E[k2X−k5Y|Y]=0 and E[k3Y−k6Z|Z]=0. Thus speeds are orthogonal regression residuals, giving three exact variance-energy decompositions, including E[Ẋ²]=Var(Φ(Z))−k4²Var X, E[Ẏ²]=k2² Var X−k5² Var Y, E[Ż²]=k3² Var Y−k6² Var Z. Stationarity of centered products XZ and YZ yields relations for covariances; eliminate C_XZ and C_XY to obtain k2 k3 Cov(Z,Φ(Z))=k6(k4+k6)(k5+k6)Var Z−k3²(k4+k5+k6)Var Y. Hill Φ strictly decreases for Z≥0; Cov(Z,Φ(Z))=1/2 E[(Z−Z′)(Φ(Z)−Φ(Z′))]<0 whenever Var Z>0; if Z constant, the stationary equations force all coordinates constant, unique equilibrium. Therefore strict sharpened VarY>k6(k4+k6)(k5+k6)/(k3²(k4+k5+k6)) VarZ for non-equilibrium; its improvement over direct filter k6²/k3² is 1+k4k5/[k6(k4+k5+k6)]>1. Re-derived covariance elimination and factor symbolically, with 9/500 versus 1/100 at printed Ruoff rates and 4/3 for equal downstream rates.

originality.rationale: Two primary same-model full texts were compared at statement and implication level. Ruoff–Rensing 1996 prints the identical three ODEs with Hill exponent nine and discusses period, phase shifts, temperature compensation, and limit-cycle parameters; its full 11-page text has no covariance/variance or invariant-measure theorem. The complete later Hill-feedback analysis studies onset and persistence of oscillations, not all-invariant-measure conditional regressions or the exact three-stage attenuation factor. Their model equations alone support stationary moment algebra, but no inspected prior stronger moment identity was found; explicit residual risk remains that the computation is known in stationary moment/control literature.
residual_risks: A more general stationary moment identity in dynamical control theory may imply the package under unrecognized naming; no comprehensive completed semantic index.
